locator: How to Apply a Tourniquet; Windlass Rod Tourniquet
baseline_support: Apply a commercial tourniquet high and tight on an extremity (never over a joint), tighten until bleeding stops, note the application time, and leave it in place for EMS.
current_support: Place the device 2–3 inches toward the torso from the wound, between wound and heart, clear of joints. Tighten until bleeding stops and leave in place for medical personnel.
conditions: Life-threatening extremity bleeding, visible wound, suitable commercial device
limitations: Identify a visible wound and follow the exact device and training. This is not the tactical high-and-tight rule or a pediatric device-fit approval.
conflict: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_origin: Governs extremity hemorrhage escalation and strict EMS handoff documentation.
audit_note: Red Cross gives visible-wound placement, joint exclusion and leaving in place. Tactical placement and pediatric fit separate.

locator: 10 Adult Foreign-Body Airway Obstruction, sections 10.1–10.3
baseline_support: Encourage forceful coughing if the person can cough or speak; activate 911 immediately for silent inability to breathe or speak and follow trained/dispatcher-guided airway-clearing care.

audit_note: AHA sections 10.1–10.3 distinguish effective cough, severe signs, unresponsiveness and exceptions. Pediatric protocol separate.

locator: How to escape a rip current
baseline_support: Rip currents are narrow fast-moving channels pulling seaward; do NOT fight directly against the current—stay calm, float or tread water, swim parallel to the shoreline out of the narrow channel and angle back to shore (or float and wave/yell for help).
current_support: Do not fight the current. Float or tread water and signal for help. Swim out across the flow only if able and conditions permit.
conditions: Caught in a rip current on a surf beach
limitations: The current, shoreline, flotation and ability vary. A universal escape direction and visual diagnosis are unsafe.
conflict: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_origin: Core coastal surf and Great Lakes rip-current card evidence.
audit_note: Primary boundary narrowed in A02. Existing broad uses remain in scope for specialist review. A01: NWS primary FAQ supports flotation and conditional exit. Avoid overriding local hazards with a fixed exit direction.

limitations: A first receding or modest wave is often followed by much larger destructive surges.
